method: Deterministic summary of computed figures. No language model is used.
national: One Nation led national search interest in the week to 25 November, averaging 47.0 on Google's 0-100 scale, 3.9 times the next party (the Greens). That is 64% of all search interest across the parties tracked.
One Nation rose the most on the previous week, up 12.1 points (+35%).
Searches for the Greens jumped to 11 on 20 November, 2.1 times the previous week's average. Coverage around that day: “Hadley: Stop Greens’ Aboriginal identity rort now” (The Daily Telegraph).
victoria: Across the latest poll from each of 8 pollsters, the Coalition averages 32.1% of the primary vote, Labor 21.3%, One Nation 21.4% and the Greens 14.5%. On two-party-preferred the Coalition leads 57.4 to 42.6 (7 polls), a 12.4-point swing to the Coalition since 2022.
Applied uniformly to the 2022 pendulum, that swing points to a Coalition majority (66 seats, 45 needed). Treat this as the classic two-party read only: it cannot see One Nation winning seats.
The YouGov MRP (November 2026), which models seats one by one, projects Coalition 110, Labor 13, One Nation 12 and Greens 8: a majority.
Preferred premier (DemosAU/Premier National, 21–25 Nov 2026): Wilson 36%, Carroll 28%, Pickering 15%.
